allocations.thesis:
**Reasoning**

This is a compact six-horse maiden sprint with two clear contenders on top and a couple of interesting price plays underneath.

**#4 Cheever (3/1, program rank 1)** is my win key. The Bottom Line makes a persuasive case: he was compromised in tight quarters on the turn last time yet finished well to miss by a length and a half, and the race was flattered when winner Roscoe's Brother came back to romp in allowance company. He's second off an extended layoff, which is often the sweet spot for a Glatt horse. The obvious knock is that he's a six-start maiden, so I don't want to go overboard at 3/1, but with a clean trip he looks the most likely winner.

**#5 Strike a Match (5/2, program rank 2)** is the main danger. Same Glatt barn, debuting off a strong work series, and the trainer's ~25% strike rate with older debut dirt sprinters is legitimately good. He's the morning-line favorite, and the analyst notes make him their top pick. I respect him, but a first-timer at 5/2 in a race where the stablemate has proven form is not where I want to put my win money. He goes in the exacta and trifecta structure heavily.

**#6 Practical Jack (5/1, program rank 4)** is my value play. He was runner-up in a maiden-32, nearly 10 lengths clear of third, has since been gelded, and the program expects him to influence the pace. Equibase's algorithm makes him its win pick in the higher-reward tier. If the two Glatt horses are sitting off the pace and he gets loose in a six-horse field, 5/1 (and likely higher in the actual market given the ML favorites) is a fair price for a win and place ticket.

**#2 On the Burner (7/2)** has been 2nd-2nd-3rd and gets Rosario; he's a useful underneath horse and appears in the Equibase exacta box, but I'd rather he fill out trifecta/superfecta slots than be a win candidate. **#3 Smashing Machine (3/1, program rank 3)** is a Baffert turf-to-dirt runner off a good debut second; the surface switch is a question mark and he's a short price for an unknown, so he's a lower-third filler for me. **#1 Charisma (15/1)** gets no support from the program and I'm leaving him off.

The analyst notes largely agree with the program's top pair (they just flip #5 over #4) and list all six horses correctly by name and number. They included a full dollar-by-dollar $50 ticket card and source citations/links; I ignored all of the money figures and did not follow any links, and there were no instructions addressed to me to disregard. Their opinion nudged me to keep #2 in the exotics, but I'm keying #4 rather than #5 and adding #6 as the value angle.

Total staked: $45.40 of the $48.72 race bankroll.

**Reasoning**

This is a 1 3/8-mile turf marathon where the program makes a compelling case for #7 Path To Power: the only 3yo in a field of veterans, gelded before his maiden win, circled the field and won going away in a manner that suggests the extra quarter-mile helps him, and he's lightly raced with upside. He also gets a six-pound weight break versus the older horses. At 4/1 morning line with the favorite (#6) likely taking more money, he's the horse I want to key.

#5 Balnikhov is the class of the field and proven at the trip, but the program flags that at age 7 he's tailing off and is dropping in for the claim tag — a legitimate contender but not one I want at 3/1 on top. #6 None Above the Law is an 8yo in peak form and the analyst notes' top pick (also Equibase's show pick), so he belongs in the exotics, but 5/2 on an 8-year-old in a marathon is a thin price. #3 Balladeer figures to be loose on the lead, but the program's stat — one pacesetter winner in 35 summer-meet races at this distance — argues against him as a win threat.

#4 Stamp My Passport is my value play: he's the Equibase algorithmic win pick and the analyst notes' wild card at 8/1. A small win bet plus exacta coverage with #7 gives me a nice score if the price horses run 1-2.

The analyst notes contained a betting card with dollar amounts and cited URLs; I ignored the money figures and did not follow any links. All horses named in the notes match entries in this race with correct numbers. I take their opinion on #6 and #4 as one more source; my structure leans on #7 with #4 as the price angle, and #5/#6 underneath.

**Analysis**

This is a seven-horse maiden dirt sprint, and the shape of the race is fairly clear from the program notes: #3 Cherry Cider is the lone controlling speed, #4 First Or Last is the most likely to press her, and #1 Street Swindler and #7 Convo are the improving second-start-back types.

My concern with the program's top choice, #3 Cherry Cider, is that she's returning from an eight-month layoff, is being asked to win gate-to-wire against a proven presser, and (per the notes) carries a long string of losses. Baffert first-off-the-layoff maidens with fast works get overbet at Del Mar; 4/1 is not a price I need to take on a horse whose only path is the front end.

#4 First Or Last is the logical winner. She ran second in a fast turf maiden sprint on debut, is trained by the meet's leading trainer in wins and starters (O'Neill), and both Equibase and the analyst notes flag her as the horse most ready to win. At 5/2 she's fair, not generous, but she's the anchor of my exotics.

#1 Street Swindler is the value. The program's own Bottom Line calls her the upset candidate: she chased and tired at 6.5f on debut, cuts back to 6f, and second-time starters routinely move up. The analyst notes make her their top pick at 6/1, which I treat as one more opinion in agreement with the program's third choice. If the 6/1 holds anywhere close, she's the win bet of the race.

#7 Convo (third in her comeback, Rosario) is a legitimate third piece and is Equibase's show pick; I'll use her in the trifecta and as an exacta partner. #2 High Society U is the analyst notes' fourth choice, but with no program rank and no Equibase support I'll leave her off rather than spread thin. #5 and #6 only appear in the algorithmic Equibase box and get no support elsewhere — I pass on them.

The notes contained a full ticket structure and dollar amounts; I ignored all of that and sized only against the $47.82 race bankroll. No horse in the notes was from another race, and all names matched their program numbers.

**Plan:** win bets on #1 (value) and #4 (logical), an exacta box #1/#4, a saver exacta box #4/#7, small exactas with #3 underneath, and a 50c four-horse trifecta box #1,#4,#7,#3 to catch the speed hanging on for a piece.

**Race 4 analysis**

The program, Equibase, and the analyst notes all converge on the same shape: #7 On the Whim is the horse to beat. He's a multiple stakes winner (Cal Dreamin at this course and distance last month), 2-for-4 over the Del Mar turf, still eligible for this first allowance condition, and the pace setup is soft – the only other confirmed speed is #1 Shamrock Glitter, a stretch-out sprinter on the rail returning from a layoff and a gelding. On the Whim can sit right off that horse or take it and control the race. At 5/2 he's a fair favorite, not a steal, but he's the logical key.

For the second slot I lean slightly toward #2 Lyle The Crocodile over #5 El Rey Rey. Both exit the same race, but Lyle was making his first start in six months and split the field – the classic second-off-the-layoff improver – and Equibase's algorithm actually makes him the higher-reward win pick. El Rey Rey ran a deceptively good second in a speed-favoring race but is on his third start of the meet, so a form-hold question exists; he still belongs in the exotics. #3 Knight To King (4/1, no program rank) gets a mention from the notes as a layoff contender – I'll use him underneath only. #1 Shamrock Glitter is the pace longshot; if the closers can't get to On the Whim, the front-runner behind him could hang on for a piece, so he's a small exacta/tri saver at 6/1. #4 Irish Prophet gets one exacta saver only because Equibase includes him. #6 Sir Percival at 15/1 with first-time blinkers doesn't show enough to spend on.

The analyst notes aligned with my read on #7 and were useful on #3 as an under-horse; I ignored the $50 card and all stake amounts in it, and did not follow any of the reference links. Every horse named in the notes matches an entry in this race.

Bankroll $46.22; staking $46 total, keyed on #7 with Lyle as the value alternative.

**Reasoning**

This is a wide-open field of 2-year-old maidens, and the two strongest structural angles both point to the Peter Miller barn. My top choice is #11 Another Warrior: he's a second-time starter who chased a fast pace and cracked in his debut, which is the classic "learned something" profile. Miller's second-out maidens improve frequently, the colt has worked well since, and meet-leading rider Joel Rosario stays aboard rather than jumping ship — a meaningful signal. He's the program's top pick and sits in the Equibase exacta box too, and at 5/1 he's a fair win price.

Stablemate #7 Character is the 3/1 morning-line favorite and the program says he looks "live," but the Bottom Line also hands us the key negative: Miller/Hernandez are 1-for-25 with first-time starters over five years. I won't fade him outright, but I don't want to take a short price on a debut runner with that stat hanging over him — he's an exotics horse for me, not a win bet.

#5 Cigar and Espresso (4/1, Rispoli) is my second win play and the horse most sources agree on as a solid contender — Equibase's show pick and part of its box, and the analyst notes' "safest alternative." #10 High Ambition is Equibase's algorithmic win pick at 5/1 and rounds out my trifecta box.

The analyst notes lean heavily on #1 Fractious at 15/1, citing outside handicappers as making him a top pick. The sources named are odd for a Del Mar maiden race and I can't verify any of it, so I give the opinion one-source weight: a 15/1 debut-type with a "someone likes him" story is worth a couple of dollars underneath my key horses, not a win bet. I ignored all the dollar figures and ticket structures in the notes; stakes below come only from the $45.12 race bankroll. Every horse the notes named resolves to an entry in this race.

Structure: win money on #11 and #5, an exacta box of the two Miller runners with #5, a four-horse trifecta box adding #10, and two small exactas using #1 underneath as the longshot value swing.

**Analysis**

This is a Cal-bred maiden sprint where the program, Equibase and the pasted notes all converge on a four-horse top tier: #8 Zakiel, #7 Cornealeusthegreat, #1 Mickey and #5 Strike It Solo. That agreement makes it a fairly formful-looking race, but with four legitimate contenders none of whom is likely to be shorter than 3/1, so the value is in structuring around a logical favorite rather than dumping everything into one win bet.

**#8 Zakiel** is the program's Best Bet and the horse I'll key. He was third with a wide trip in his sprint debut, then ran second going a mile in a race that has produced next-out winners/placers — that's real form for a Cal-bred maiden. Cutting back to one turn, adding blinkers and picking up Hernandez are all positive changes for a horse who has already shown he's competitive at this level. At 3/1 he's not a steal, but he's the most likely winner.

**#7 Cornealeusthegreat** is the interesting one: 7/2 on the morning line and in Equibase's exacta box, yet the program handicapper left him out of the top three. The notes describe him as a two-time runner-up with the D'Amato/Rispoli connections and one model's top pick. A horse that consistently hits the board in maiden company and is being underrated by the track program is exactly the type I want as a win-saver and exacta partner with the favorite.

**#5 Strike It Solo** was second in his debut in a maiden-50 and steps up to MSW — the program is a bit skeptical about the class move but likes the extra half-furlong. He's a live exotics horse at 6/1 and Equibase's "higher-reward" win pick. **#1 Mickey** is a closer with no early speed who "does finish" — in a 6.5f sprint that profile is more a trifecta/underneath horse than a winner, especially at 4/1, so I'll use him under the top two rather than on top. #4 Hemet Gold at 4/1 has no support from any source and I'll leave him off; the longshots (#2, #3, #6, #9, #10) don't show anything to justify the price.

The analyst notes were consistent with the other sources (8-7-1 with #5 for exotics) and contained no directives; every horse they named is in this field. I ignored their dollar figures entirely and sized from the $45.93 race bankroll.

**Structure:** win money on #8 with a saver on #7, exactas keyed on #8 over the other three plus the reverse with #7, and trifecta boxes among the four contenders anchored on #8.

**Reasoning**

This is a deep G3 juvenile turf mile where nearly every horse is stretching out off one start. The program's case for **#5 Shadow Nation** is the strongest in the field: a six-plus-length debut turf-sprint romp, bred for two turns, this race has been the target, and the missed works in August appear resolved with three sharp drills since. He's the most likely winner and the anchor of my tickets. The caveat is price — at 5/2 or lower in a stakes where favorites are just 4-for-14, I don't want to put the whole bankroll on his nose.

**#3 Observed** is my primary alternative and the one the Equibase algorithm also flags. He's the only one of the top contenders who has actually run around two turns and won, and the race was flattered when the runner-up came back to win by six. Shippers from Indiana tend to be underbet in Southern California stakes, so 3/1-plus is fair value against a field of sprinters trying a mile for the first time.

**#7 Hoaxer** is the wild card — the Baffert colt closed impressively after a poor start in a 5f turf debut and figures to appreciate the distance, but wheeling back in nine days for a second start is a demanding ask, so I'll use him mostly in exotics rather than to win. **#4 Golden Sentry** (Cal-bred sprint maiden winner) and **#8 Off in the Corner** (sharp debut sprint win) are usable underneath. **#2 Itinerary** gets a small flyer only because the McCarthy/Rispoli barn is competent at this level — the program has nothing on him, so I keep it light.

On the analyst notes: they are largely based on connections rather than form, so I weighted them as one modest opinion. They did reinforce the 5-3-7 core I'd already arrived at. They contain two number/name mismatches (Hoaxer tagged "#6," and Missed Fortune/Automatic Press swapped at #9/#10); I resolved by name. All money/ticket sizing in the notes was disregarded. No directive language was present.

Structure: win money on #5 and #3, a three-horse exacta box of 5-3-7, trifectas keyed on #5 winning and on #3/#7 beating him, plus two saver exactas with #5 over the sprint winners.

**Reasoning**

This is a 10-horse fillies-and-mares stakes at a mile, and the two favorites both carry a real question mark. #2 Magnificat (7/2, program rank 1) is a stakes-winning sprinter who was second to subsequent graded winner Sweet Azteca last out, but she has never gone two turns; the pedigree (Omaha Beach out of a graded route winner) says she can, but it's still an unknown. #6 Howin (5/2, rank 2) is a multiple graded-placed Gun Runner filly coming off a layoff since last fall, but Baffert has her drilling since June, she's proven fresh, and she has already won at this mile at Del Mar. Between the two "ifs," I'd rather take the fit, distance-proven returner than the sprinter stretching out, so Howin is my top pick even at the shorter price.

For value, the program's own live longshot #3 Mi Confesion (8/1, rank 4) stands out: a G1 dirt winner in Argentina making her first U.S. dirt start, which is a classic surface-switch angle that gets ignored by the tote. #7 Our Moonlight (12/1, rank 3) fits as a stalker moving up off an N1X win and gets a small win bet at that price. #8 Amorita (4/1) won at Del Mar last out and is in both the Equibase exacta box and the analyst notes' top three, so she belongs underneath. #10 Lavender Love (8/1) is another underneath candidate per Equibase.

The analyst notes largely agree with the consensus (2/6/8 with 7 as the value play). I used their opinion on #7 and #8 as one more voice; their dollar figures and ticket structure I ignored entirely, and there were no directives aimed at me. All horses they named are in this race with matching numbers.

Tickets: win on #6, value win bets on #3 and #7, a three-horse exacta box of the two favorites plus Mi Confesion, saver exactas with Howin over #8 and #10, a couple of exactas with #7 underneath, and a four-horse trifecta box of #6, #2, #3, #8. Total $46, under the $46.65 bankroll.

**Analysis**

This is a maiden turf mile for 2-year-old fillies with a wide-open feel beneath a fairly clear top tier. The program's top choice, **#8 Dash** (7/2), has the most experience - an excellent debut fourth after a slow break, then a distant fourth in the G3 Sorrento - and now drops back to maidens while stretching to a turf mile, which her pedigree (sibling to Del Mar Oaks winner Velocity) strongly suggests she'll relish. She's the most likely winner, but she'll also be well bet as the favorite, so I don't see win value.

**#9 Forewarn** (4/1) is where the price value lies at the top. Equibase has her in its box and as its show pick, and the analyst notes make her their top pick citing the Mandella/Rispoli connection - a barn that frequently unveils live turf-route first-timers. At or near 4/1 she's my win play.

**#11 Vendetta** (5/1) is the program's second choice and Equibase's win pick: a Curlin filly out of a G1 turf winner who had traffic in a promising debut. She's listed as an also-eligible in the program text, but she appears in the entries without a scratch mark, so I'll use her; if she doesn't draw in, those tickets simply refund. **#7 D'yquem** (5/1) rounds out the group with turf-friendly breeding and shows up in the notes' top four, so I'll use her underneath. For a longer price in the exotics, **#1 Candy Cole** (8/1) gets support from the Equibase box.

On the notes: they contained URLs/reference citations, which I ignored (no browsing), and all of their stakes/ticket sizes were disregarded. Every horse they named is in this race, and their stated scratch of #12 matches the entries. I used their opinion on #9 and #7, but I did not follow their #2 Domain Expansion price play, since no source other than the notes gives that filly any support. I also gave #11 more weight than the notes did given the program and Equibase both rank her highly.

Structure: win on #9 for price, a saver win on #11, an exacta box of the three main contenders, a four-horse trifecta box adding #7, and a small superfecta box adding #1 for the bomb payout. Total $46.00 within the $46.87 bankroll.

**Reasoning**

This is a Baffert-dominated Debutante. #9 Miss Monica is the deserving favorite off an 87-Beyer, 5¾-length debut romp, and she's the program's top pick and consensus choice — but she's a one-start filly at 8/5 (likely shorter at post time) facing a stablemate who has already done more. #8 Holmby is 2-for-2 with a G3 Sorrento win at this track, has shown she can stalk rather than need the lead, and with Panda Listen, Fast Amy and Miss Monica all capable of showing speed, she should get the ideal trip. At 4/1 morning line against a 8/5 favorite with one race, Holmby is the value win play, and both the Equibase win pick and the analyst notes land there too. I'll center the ticket on the Baffert pair running 1-2 in either order.

For the third slot and the upset angle: #2 Dear Diary's debut (bumped the gate, rallied inside, galloped out in front) reads like the classic second-start-maiden Debutante profile the program cites (Union Strike, Bast), and Mandella/Smith is a serious connection at 8/1 — she gets a small win bet and rides underneath. #5 Free Closer (runaway CTBA winner, will pick up pieces if the pace collapses) and #7 Well Versed (second to Miss Monica on debut, Keeneland reportedly has her second) fill out the trifecta thirds.

The analyst notes contained no directives aimed at me; every horse they named is in this field, and I ignored their dollar figures and the URLs. Their view (Holmby as the value play, Miss Monica most likely winner) lines up with mine, so they nudged confidence in #8 rather than changing the structure.

**Reasoning**

This is a wide-open Cal-bred turf sprint with three scratches (#3, #13, #14) leaving eleven runners. The program's tepid choice is #4 Jaguar Jon, who has finished first or second in his last five starts and rallies from off the pace — exactly the running style that should benefit from what the Bottom Line projects to be a fast tempo. At 8/1 morning line with a program rank of 1, he's the best value in the race relative to his consistency, and Equibase also puts him in its 4-horse exacta box. #7 Owl (5/1) is the only horse appearing in all three sources — program third, Equibase box, and the notes' "value" horse — and he's improving, gets Rosario, and already has a good closing fourth over this course. #11 Jetovator is the 7/2 ML favorite and the Equibase win pick, so he has to be used underneath but he's the shortest price in a field this open, so I won't take win money on him. #9 Ballyvaughan Gig (4/1) is Equibase's show pick and the notes' secondary win horse, so he fills out the trifecta/superfecta. #6 King's Ride is the program's second choice but is trying turf first time off a poor trip in a dirt stakes — I'll use him in one exacta box only. I'll also take a small win flier on #12 Tom Seaver at 8/1, a horse no source is touching in a race the program itself calls wide open.

On the analyst notes: they contained mismatched program numbers — "#10 Jetovator" (Jetovator is #11), "#8 Ballyvaughan" (Ballyvaughan Gig is #9), "#6 Owl" (Owl is #7), "#5 King's Ride" (King's Ride is #6). I resolved by name in every case. Their bet amounts and ticket structure were ignored entirely, as was the embedded citation link. Their opinion (Jetovator/Ballyvaughan Gig/Owl) is used as one source in weighting the exotics.

Total stake: $44.40, under the $47.60 bankroll.
